title: Hardware-aware provisioning and boot/network ordering playbook (work-in-progress)
summary: A practical, hardware-aware sequence and Terraform module guidance for on-prem Kubernetes cluster provisioning across heterogeneous racks (bare metal + vSphere). Focuses on boot ordering, network attachments, NIC firmware recommendations, PXE/iPXE handoff, and upgrade/rollback primitives to minimize blast radius.
body:
Purpose:
This doc captures an operational playbook for provisioning and initial bootstrap of on-prem clusters where hardware topology matters (mixed blade, rackmount, and nested vSphere hosts). It combines an opinionated boot order, network bonding plan, Terraform module wiring notes, and a safe upgrade sequence. This is intended as a living working doc (WIP) for SEs and SREs doing field installs and Private deployments.

Scope:
- Fresh installs of small-to-medium clusters (3-50 nodes) across mixed hardware types.
- Hybrid environments: direct-baremetal provisioning for worker nodes + vSphere provisioned control-plane or worker pools is common.
- Does NOT cover advanced storage backends in depth (Ceph/Longhorn notes at the end).

Assumptions and constraints:
- PXE-capable BMC or IPMI on baremetal nodes; vSphere inventory reachable from provisioning network; OR air-gapped installs using pre-burned images for nodes.
- Dedicated provisioning network (VLAN/provisioning subnet) with DHCP + TFTP/HTTP for iPXE artifacts.
- Centralized Terraform control-plane (run from ops laptop or Jenkins) with credentials for vSphere and out-of-band management APIs.
- Default bootstrap tool: kubeadm for control plane, but notes for Talos / Rancher RKE2 in sections below.

High-level sequence (canonical order) - hardware-aware:
1) Validate rack topology (inventory CSV) and classify nodes into roles: control-plane (CP), edge-control-plane (optional), workers, infra/monitoring, storage-only.
2) On-provision networking: create provisioning VLAN, BGP/EVPN routes to aggregation switches, and isolated DHCP for PXE.
3) Prepare Terraform modules for inventory: modules/baremetal-provisioner, modules/vsphere-host, modules/networking-provision. Map inventory CSV -> tfvars.
4) Flash BIOS/NIC firmware baseline on baremetal (if possible) and set PXE priority. Document NIC model and firmware per rack.
5) Deploy provisioning services (matchbox or iPXE HTTP server) on ephemeral VM in provisioning network.
6) Boot order enforcement: BMC -> iPXE -> netboot installer -> fetch ignition/cloud-init. Control-plane nodes should be booted first in a staggered pattern (one at a time for initial CPs) to avoid quorum issues.
7) Kubeadm control-plane init with stacked etcd (or external etcd per customer preference). Apply CNI (Calico/Calico-IPAM or Cilium) pinned to data-plane parameters.
8) Join workers after CPs healthy. Verify KV cache, node labels, and resource topology awareness.
9) Apply storage class and CSI; run e2e smoke checks and application test harness.

Boot ordering details and rationale:
- Staggered CP init: bring up first CP and confirm etcd leader election, then second with delay 300s, then third. Reason: reduce split-brain risk on crowded provisioning networks and avoid multiple simultaneous etcd startups which can saturate disks on older nodes.
- Bonding and NIC configuration: prefer LACP-bond active-backup for mgmt/provisioning network to avoid link flap issues; for data-plane, prefer LACP balance-tcp if switches support it. Use consistent MTU across provisioning and data VLANs (recommend 9000 only if storage network tested).
- vSphere nested nodes: power on vSphere hosts only after control-plane network routes are validated. vSphere template must include cloud-init that hits the provisioning HTTP endpoint for kubejoin.

Terraform module notes (practical knobs):
- modules/baremetal-provisioner: expects variables: inventory_csv, provisioning_network_id, ipmi_creds_secret, pxe_image_url. Outputs: node_meta map with macs, desired_role, final_boot_action.
- modules/vsphere-host: common knobs: template_name, folder, resource_pool, network_map (map of logical network -> portgroup). Expose custom attribute cluster_role to tag hosts for provisioning pipeline.
- modules/networking-provision: create VLAN, dhcp_scope, switch_acls var (list of ACL blocks). Provide a dry-run flag (plan_only) so infra folks can validate without pushing to devices.
- state considerations: keep separate tfstate per site/rack to limit blast radius. Use locking (consul/remote state backend).

Preflight checklist (run before hitting ON button):
- Inventory CSV validated: no duplicate MACs, serials present.
- Out-of-band (BMC/iDRAC/iLO) reachable and credentials working.
- Provisioning server reachable from BMC network.
- DHCP scope not overlapping production IPs.
- vSphere APIs accessible and template checksum matches expected.
- SSH key injection tested for the template.

Upgrade and rollback strategy (control plane + nodes):
- Upgrade policy: control-plane first, then kube-proxy/CNI, then workers grouped by rack/affinity. Never upgrade all nodes in a rack simultaneously.
- Safe window: limit concurrent CP upgrades to 1 (unless using external etcd with more than 3 members).
- Terraform-driven node replacement: for kernel/firmware upgrades prefer replace path: cordon -> drain -> mark_pxe_reimage variable in tfstate for that host -> re-provision -> kubejoin -> uncordon. This keeps image and firmware steps atomic and auditable.
- Rollback: keep known-good images in iPXE server and a documented tfvar set tag:reimage_target=stable-YYYYMMDD. If new image fails health checks, flip an automated tag to reimage back to stable.

Edge cases and resilience:
- Single-tenant racks with limited BMC throughput: add 10s delay between PXE handoffs; monitor BMC job queue.
- Mixed disk performance (NVMe + SATA): ensure etcd placement on faster nodes or use isolated fast disks for etcd volumes. Avoid provisioning CP on slow disk nodes.
- Intermittent DHCP collisions: fall back to pre-provisioned static IP mapping stored in Terraform vars.

Commands and snippets (examples):
- Example tfvars mapping for inventory: inventory_csv = "site1-rackA-inventory-20241010.csv"
- Kick off provisioning (terraform): 
  terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=site1.tfvars && terraform apply -var-file=site1.tfvars
- Quick node reimage flow (operator): 
  # mark host for reimage in terraform vars -> apply
  # watchdog: monitor provisioning server logs and the node BMC serial console for success.

Testing and validation:
- Health checks: kube-apiserver up, etcd CTL cluster-health, node kubelet ready, CNI pod-to-pod ping across nodes.
- Perf smoke: run 100-pod churn test with typical workload to verify scheduling and binpack heuristics with the hardware topology plugin.
- Storage smoke: create PVCs and validate IO latency under load.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Consider adding explicit BIOS tuning guide per NIC vendor (Intel X710 vs Broadcom 57414) — need to collect recommended settings from HW team.
- Investigate automated firmware upgrade via Redfish in terraform module (auth flow and rate limiting).
- Decide on default for MTU: 1500 vs 9000. Need customer guidance doc.

Appendix A: Minimal ignition/cloud-init payload example (kubeadm join snippet)
- Provided as pointer to github repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/provisioning/cloudinit-examples (linked above).

Appendix B: Short checklist for field engineers
- Print a single side laminated checklist: BMC creds, PXE server IP, DHCP scope, first CP serial, expected etcd leader.

Appendix C: Quick remediation flow for failed CP init
1) Capture journalctl -u kubelet and kubeadm logs on host console.
2) If etcd membership inconsistent: follow etcd recovery play (snapshot restore) described in CONFLUENCE-1234.
3) If disk IO saturation suspected: migrate CP to different rack or attached faster disk image and rejoin.

Notes and references:
- Link to Terraform modules: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/modules/baremetal-provisioner
- Network design reference: CONFLUENCE-NET/OnPrem-Design
- Related field runbooks: field-deploy-lab-iso-factory-notes.json (see Drive)

End of WIP playbook.
Unresolved items are marked in the Open questions section — please add notes directly in this doc and ping #private-deploy to sync on changes.
